name: Haran
overview: Haran is a male biblical figure identified primarily as the son of Terah, as recorded in Genesis 11:26. Beyond this unique attribute, Scripture provides limited additional personal details about him. His role is noted within the early genealogical records of the patriarchal lineage.
namesAndTitles: The name Haran means 'mountaineer,' a proper name noted in Genesis 11:27. This name does not appear to be given by God but reflects a common personal designation in the biblical narrative.
familyAndRelationships: Haran is explicitly recorded as the father of Lot, Milcah, and Iscah, establishing him as a significant progenitor in the Genesis account (Genesis 11:27, 29). He is also inferred to be the son of Terah, connecting him directly to the ancestral line of Abraham.
scriptureSignificance: Haran's significance lies in his position within the ancestral genealogy leading to key biblical figures such as Abraham and Lot. As the father of Lot, his lineage directly impacts the unfolding narrative of God's covenant people. While not much else is detailed about his life, his mention anchors important family connections foundational to the biblical story.
